Fully-funded PhD in Music (Computational Musicology)

University of Bristol

Qualification Type: PhD
Location: Bristol
Funding for: UK Students
Funding amount: £21,805 UKRI Standard Stipend Amount
Hours: Full Time
Placed On: 16th November 2026
Closes: 6th January 2027

Location: Victoria Rooms, University of Bristol

The project:

Project Description

PhD studentship within the ERC-funded Anonymous Agency project, Department of Music, University of Bristol. https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101264213.

Old Hispanic chant is preserved in unpitched notation, which communicates note count, syllable underlay, and contour (but not precise intervals or pitches). The repertoire’s musical grammar is well understood, but among the thousands of extant chants can we discern chronological layers, distinct communities of practice or even individual (anonymous) authorship?

This PhD will harness machine learning approaches to explore these questions, drawing on the ca. 3000 melodies already in machine-readable format (see https://neumes.org.uk/view for published examples). The student will be trained to transcribe further chants, as necessary. (S)he might focus on particular chant genres, or on specific feasts, types of feasts, or liturgical seasons. 

Essential criteria

  • Masters degree, completed or to be completed by September 2027, in Computer Science or Musicology or a related discipline.
  • English as first language, or Profile B English language skills (further information: https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/language-requirements/)
  • Programming skills (e.g. LeetCode rating of 1500+, Computer Science qualification at A level or above, or equivalent experience).
  • A demonstrated interest in early music, chant or liturgy.
  • Potential to communicate technical methodology to a non-specialist audience.

Desirable criteria

  • Solid background in hypothesis testing and data analysis, to undertake probabilistic modelling.

How to apply:

Before applying, please check the entry requirements.

You must provide the following in your application:

  • A CV
  • Two referees (add to the Reference section of your application form)
  • A personal statement highlighting your motivation for applying for this PhD, and any relevant experience and/or skills (maximum of one side of A4, font size 11).
  • Degree certificates and transcripts
  • Evidence of meeting the English Language profile
  • A research statement/proposal (1000 words)

Application Process

Before applying, please contact Emma.Hornby@bristol.ac.uk with preliminary ideas for a research proposal. You will be given informal feedback on this before making the formal application. You may also apply for a Bristol Postgraduate Research Scholarship (but will only be permitted to hold one scholarship if successful in both competitions): https://www.bristol.ac.uk/arts-law-social-sciences/postgraduate-research/bristol-pg-research-scholarships-alss/ Shortlisted candidates for the Anonymous Agency studentship will be given an analytical technical exercise as part of the selection process.

Online applications are made via the above ‘Apply’ button. Please select PhD in Music on the Programme Choice page. You will be prompted to enter details of the studentship in the Funding and Research Details sections of the form.

Candidate requirements:  

Funding: Four-year scholarship. The minimum tax-free stipend at the UKRI rate is £21,805 for 2026/27. For eligibility and residence requirements please check the UK Research and Innovation website.

Up to an additional £2100 per year will be available from the Anonymous Agency project to support fieldwork and conference attendance. All expenses will be covered for a training semester in Prague, including travel and accommodation. The training will be provided by Dr Jan Hajič jr. (Institute of Formal and Applied Linguistics, Charles University, Prague) 

Contacts: Project-specific queries: Emma.Hornby@bristol.ac.uk

Application queries: uob-pgradmissions@bristol.ac.uk
